meta.title: Strong leader
meta.question: Would a strong leader unconstrained by parliament be good for Poland?
meta.measure: Average position on executive power, from 0 (a constrained executive) to 10 (a strong leader unconstrained by parliament)
meta.anchor: Pooled from questions on whether a strong leader would do more for the country than laws, parliament and elections, with every answer placed on 0 to 10 and the trend read on the scale of an average question.

items.wording: If the situation in the country does not improve: introducing strong-hand rule and giving up democracy (agree ... disagree)
items.notes: CBOS, January 1992 to January 1995, 6 surveys (4-point); the May 1993 file labels its 'completely disagree' code 'Całkowicie zgadzam' and fails the check.

items.wording: Poland now needs a strong leader who will bring order to the country (agree-disagree)
items.notes: CBOS, March 1992, 1 survey.

items.wording: Introducing strong-hand rule and giving up democracy (5-point: fully agree ... fully disagree, middle 'undecided')
items.notes: CBOS, August 1995, 1 survey: the 5-point version of CBOS_STRONG_HAND.

items.wording: A strong leader can do more for the country than laws, discussions and votes (agree-disagree)
items.notes: CBOS, 1995-2015. From 24 October 2026 coded in the collapsed form CBOS's reports print (no 'definitely'/'rather' split), in the microdata as in the reports of 2018-2026, so that the item is one series to 2026.

items.wording: A good leader does not need to obey the law (agree-disagree)
items.notes: POLPAN 1998, 2003, 2008, 2013 and 2018: 5 waves. 2013 asked in one questionnaire version (about four fifths of the sample). The rule-unbound leader of PGSW_STRONG_LEADER.

items.wording: Elections are not necessary if leaders represent the interests of citizens (agree-disagree)
items.notes: POLPAN 1998, 2003, 2008, 2013 and 2018: 5 waves (the 1998 label is shortened). 2013 in one questionnaire version (most of the sample). A leader who need not bother with elections.

items.wording: Having a strong leader who does not have to bother with parliament and elections: a very good, fairly good, fairly bad or very bad way of governing Poland?
items.notes: European Values Study 1999, 2008 and 2017, 3 surveys (not asked in 1990).

items.wording: From the point of view of utility, do we need a parliament for things to go well, or can we do without it?
items.notes: Consolidation of Democracy in CEE, January 1991 and March 2000, 2 surveys.

items.wording: Own position: Poland governed by an eminent leader who understands the will of the people (0) vs by cooperating democratic institutions (10)
items.notes: PGSW 2000 presidential study (SINGLE), 1 survey. The leader pole also carries a populist note ('understands the will of the people').

items.wording: Should we rely on a democratic form of government to solve our country's problems, or on a leader with a strong hand?
items.notes: Pew Global Attitudes 2002, 2007, 2009 (fall) and 2016: 4 surveys with Polish answers (the question is in other files but not asked in Poland).

items.wording: Having a strong leader who does not have to bother with parliament and elections (very good ... very bad)
items.notes: World Values Survey Poland 2005 and 2012, 2 surveys (absent from the 1989 and 1997 Polish files).

items.wording: A strong leader who does not have to bother with parliament and elections: a good or bad way to govern Poland?
items.notes: PGSW 2015.

items.wording: A system in which a strong leader can make decisions without interference from parliament or the courts: a very good ... very bad way of governing Poland?
items.notes: Pew Global Attitudes 2017, 2023 and 2024, 3 surveys.

items.wording: Having a strong leader in government is good for Poland even if the leader bends the rules to get things done (agree-disagree)
items.notes: European Election Study 2019 (online), 1 survey; the same item as EES_STRONG_LEADER (2024) and PGSW_STRONG_LEADER.

items.wording: A strong leader is good for Poland even if they bend the rules to get things done (agree-disagree)
items.notes: PGSW 2019 and 2023.

items.wording: Rule by a strong leader who does not have to reckon with parliament and voters: a very good ... very bad political system?
items.notes: SWPS COVID tracker waves 3, 5 and 9 (April-June 2020), 3 surveys; online.

items.wording: The authorities may break the rules of democracy if the interest of society requires it (yes/no)
items.notes: SWPS COVID tracker waves 4, 6, 9 and 15 (April 2020 to November 2021), 4 surveys; online. Wave 15 names it Q46_1.

items.wording: Is 'strong-hand' rule, more powers for the executive, a good way to improve the situation in Poland (0), or rather a bigger role for representative bodies such as local government (10)?
items.notes: SWPS COVID tracker wave 13 (March 2021), 1 survey; online. The representative pole names local government, not parliament.

items.wording: The government should be able to bend the law to solve pressing social and political problems (agree-disagree)
items.notes: NCN Opus online panel, waves 1-3, 3 surveys (copies A1_P_*, EQLAW1_*).

items.wording: If parliament obstructs the government's work, it should be ignored (agree-disagree)
items.notes: NCN Opus online panel, waves 1-3 (spring 2023, autumn 2023, spring 2024), 3 surveys of the same panel; wave 3 asked about half. The files hold identical copies (A1_N_*, LEGCNSTR1_*); the first is used.

items.wording: Rule by a strong leader who does not have to reckon with parliament and voters: a very good ... very bad way of governing the country?
items.notes: NCN Opus online panel, waves 1 and 3, 2 surveys; the EVS/WVS/PGSW 2015 wording.

items.wording: A strong leader can do more for the country than laws, discussions and votes (agree-disagree)
items.notes: CBOS's mixed-mode surveys (CAPI, CATI or CAWI, the respondent's choice) from APiW 359 (May-June 2020), so a question of its own.

items.wording: A strong leader is good for Poland even if they bend the rules (agree-disagree)
items.notes: European Election Study 2024.

items.wording: The government should be able to bend the law to solve pressing social and political problems (agree-disagree)
items.notes: FNW SWPS online survey, May 2025, 1 survey; label in decomposed Unicode, so the regex avoids Polish letters.

items.wording: If parliament obstructs the government's work, it should be ignored (agree-disagree)
items.notes: FNW SWPS online survey, May 2025, 1 survey (coded the other way round from NCN). The file stores this label in decomposed Unicode (NFD), so the regex avoids Polish letters.

items.wording: Strong leaders should be able to make decisions without interference from the courts or parliament (agree-disagree)
items.notes: FNW SWPS online survey, December 2025, 1 survey.

items.wording: The government should be able to bend the law to solve pressing social and political problems (agree-disagree)
items.notes: BDCS survey, Poland 2025 (SINGLE), 1 survey.

items.wording: If there is no consensus in parliament, the government should be able to use executive decrees to pass laws (agree-disagree)
items.notes: BDCS survey, Poland 2025 (SINGLE), 1 survey.

items.wording: If the national parliament obstructs the government's work, it should be ignored (agree-disagree)
items.notes: BDCS survey, Poland 2025 (SINGLE), 1 survey.

items.wording: Governments have the right to weaken institutions that limit their executive power (agree-disagree)
items.notes: BDCS survey, Poland 2025 (SINGLE), 1 survey.
